slides.heading: COLOR TEMPERATURE
slides.subheading: Match all lights to one color temperature

slides.heading: WHY IT MATTERS
bullets: Color temperature defines the warmth or coolness of light
Consistent color temperature makes grading easier and cleaner

slides.heading: KELVIN SCALE
slides.caption: Daylight ~5600K; tungsten ~3200K — match your lights to the dominant source.

slides.heading: HOW TO MATCH
steps: Set camera white balance to match.
Gel lights to match the environment.
Avoid mixing warm and cool sources.

slides.heading: PRO TIP
slides.text: Use warm light for intimacy and cool light for tension.

slides.heading: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.text: Ignoring practical lights that contaminate the scene.
